target_customer: Utilities, independent power producers and operators of battery energy storage systems and electrified fleets
problem: Battery owners cannot see cell level health, imbalance and safety risks in real time, which hurts safety, uptime and revenue.
business_model: B2B software licenses for on premise algorithms plus analytics services

founders.name: Shyam Srinivasan
founders.background_notes: Nearly a decade designing and manufacturing consumer electronics.

founders.name: Evan Murphy
founders.background_notes: Data infrastructure engineer; worked on Autopilot simulation at Tesla.

competitors.name: TWAICE
competitors.what: Cloud battery analytics with digital twin for EVs and storage
competitors.funding_then: 11M EUR Series A led by Creandum, March 2020

technical_complexity.rationale: Estimating state of charge, power and imbalance from cell data needs battery modeling and robust embedded and cloud software.

defensibility.rationale: Algorithms and operational data from deployed fleets compound, and on premise integration with control systems raises switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Emerson partnered with Zitara in 2025 after investing, and Fortescue's Elysia acquired it in January 2026.

market_need_then: Rapid growth of grid batteries and EVs and high profile battery fires created demand for safety and performance analytics.

branding.domain_note: Uses zitara.com; startup coverage also cites zitara.io.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and direct, short lines such as Less downtime. More money.

brand_strength.rationale: Niche B2B brand with trade press and partner mentions, now folded under Elysia from Fortescue.

outcome_analysis: Zitara built predictive battery software for storage and fleets, raised a 12M Series A in 2022 and 17M in December 2024 including Salesforce Ventures and Emerson Ventures, and partnered with Emerson in 2025. Fortescue's Elysia acquired it in January 2026 to add on site controls to its cloud analytics. Deep technical work and strategic investors led to a strategic exit.
notes: Directory status says Active while the company site and Fortescue say Zitara is now part of Elysia (acquisition, January 2026, terms undisclosed); exit recorded as acquisition. The 2024 round is labeled Series AA by some sources and the lead is cited as Salesforce Ventures by CB Insights and geo.sig.ai, so the label and lead are less certain; total funding estimates conflict (17M to 49M) and a 10M seed appears only in a garbled snippet, unverified. Founder education not found. Voltaiq competitor date unknown. Voltaiq omitted as undated.
